name: Bay Mini-Grants
summary: Annual small grants for community-led restoration and education projects in the Tampa Bay watershed, open to nonprofits, businesses, schools and some government agencies but not individuals.

steps: Selection committee review and board approval

eligibility.rule: Applicant has a FEIN or state tax exemption
Government agency applicants have a project with strong volunteer or community involvement
Project addresses one to three CCMP Actions
Private-property project has public access, an existing conservation easement, or a direct Tampa Bay link
Each applicant may submit up to two proposals and receive at most one award

applicant_types.quote: Nonprofit organizations, businesses, and educational institutions are eligible to receive grant funds. Government agencies may apply if a project has strong volunteer or community involvement.

geography.quote: Projects must be within the Tampa Bay watershed.

access.quote: Bay Mini-Grants are competitive awards that fund environmental restoration and education projects in the Tampa Bay watershed with a focus on community-led initiatives.

window.quote: The next application period will open in the summer of 2027 and will close in the fall of 2027.

amount.quote: The maximum award is $10,000 per project.

co_finance_required.quote: Matching funds are not required, but including other costs and funding can strengthen your application's competitiveness.

effort.quote: The next application period will open in the summer of 2027 and will close in the fall of 2027.
They will provide findings to the TBEP Executive Director who will make recommendations for approval to the TBEP Management and Policy Boards

eligibility.quote: A federal employer identification number (FEIN) or state tax exemption is required.
Applicant is a nonprofit organization, business, educational institution, or government agency in good standing with a valid FEID or exemption
Government agencies may apply if a project has strong volunteer or community involvement.

In the application and scope of work documents, each project must address at least one, and up to three, of the Actions listed in the Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan for Tampa Bay (CCMP).
Funds will not be awarded to projects on private property unless there is public access, an existing conservation easement, or the property has a direct link to Tampa Bay.
Applicants may submit up to two proposals, but only one proposal per organization may be awarded.

documents.quote: Complete scope of work and budget are provided
The application must include a detailed budget using the required template.
